rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> two-year (2009, 2010) split-plot field experiment at CCRI Multan, Pakistan, with drip (I1) and furrow (I2) irrigation as main plots and seven weed-management treatments as sub-plots, three replications, 7 m x 3 m plots. Q2: Results, 'Weed density' section and Table 1 <U+2013> all drip-irrigated treatments showed a significant 19-24% decrease in total weed density at 60 DAS compared with furrow irrigation (77.9 vs 102.7 m-2 in 2009; 87.5 vs 108.4 m-2 in 2010); weed dry matter also lower under drip (69.9 vs 101.3 and 84.7 vs 114.0 g m-2).
rows.notes: Q3: weed density and weed dry matter both come from the same quadrat sampling at 60 DAS <U+2013> one method. Q4: the mechanism (drip gives optimum moisture only to the crop root zone so weeds get less soil moisture) is asserted and attributed to Choudhary et al. 2012; soil moisture was not measured. Q5/Q6: single site, single crop (cotton CIM-557), plot scale; two years are not sites. Q7: no condition stated as a requirement for the weed-suppression effect. Q8: no limitations of the result are stated. Q9: Tables report LSD values and letter groupings only, which are significance thresholds rather than dispersion measures; the '19-24%' is a range across years/treatments, not an uncertainty of the estimate <U+2013> answered no with this doubt.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own two-year randomized split-plot field trial (2009-2010) at CCRI Multan comparing drip and furrow irrigation under seven weed-control treatments in cotton. Q2: Results 'Weed density' section and Table 1 <U+2013> drip irrigation reduced total weed density by 19-24% and weed dry matter (69.9/84.7 vs 101.3/114.0 g m-2) relative to furrow irrigation at 60 DAS in both years; discussion states drip and all weed-management practices significantly suppressed weed population and dry matter.
rows.notes: Same result as the first row (reduced weed growth under drip vs furrow in cotton). Q3: single sampling method (uprooting from quadrats at 60 DAS). Q4: reduced moisture availability to weeds under drip is asserted/cited (Choudhary et al. 2012), not measured. Q5/Q6: one site, one crop, plot scale. Q7: no requirement conditions stated from own findings. Q8: no limitations stated. Q9: only LSD and letter groupings reported, no SD/SE/CI; answered no.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a primary field experiment; drip vs furrow is a main-plot factor so the weed-density difference is the study's own result on drip irrigation. Note the text is a proof version with a typo in the author name (Kakoomat/Hakoomat).
